title: Why Instilling A Love Of School Should Be Your Highest Priority
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin urges teachers to make it their top priority to help students genuinely enjoy being in their classroom, arguing no other strategy motivates behavior, attention, or academic focus as powerfully. He positions curriculum as secondary to the attitude and enthusiasm a teacher cultivates, warning that boredom and dissatisfaction inevitably invite students to create their own—often disruptive—stimulation. He insists that fostering this love doesn't require extra planning, theatrical skill, or constant excitement; it is instead an attitude, expressed through humor, tone of voice, relationships, and genuine enjoyment of teaching. The piece closes with a call to keep focus on students and the act of teaching itself rather than getting lost in peripheral administrative demands.
points: No classroom management strategy motivates behavior and academic focus as powerfully as students genuinely enjoying being in the classroom.
Curriculum matters, but should take a back seat to cultivating enjoyment and a sense of community in the room.
When boredom or dissatisfaction take hold, students will manufacture their own stimulation, and misbehavior 'thrives' in that environment.
Creating an enjoyable classroom doesn't require extra planning or theatrical performance—it's an attitude expressed through tone, humor, and relationships.
Teachers should guard against losing track of the true joy of teaching amid schedules, meetings, materials, and other administrative 'peripherals.'
quotes: If you were to have only one goal this coming school year, make it that your students enjoy being in your classroom.
Instilling a love for school affects and changes students like nothing else can or ever will, improving the effectiveness of virtually everything you do.
The unavoidable truth is that when boredom and dissatisfaction take root in your classroom, your students will create their own enjoyment.
Like poison ivy amid the world’s changing climates, disrespect and misbehavior thrive in such an environment.
It is simply an attitude, a spirit, and a cultivation of enjoyment. It’s finding humor in the everyday and laughter for laughter’s sake.
The sad result is that the life and vitality of the classroom becomes lost in a forest of peripherals.
